paper_row.label: schwdef:timelike_homotopic_fixed_endpoints
paper_row.principal: Causal.Causality.FutureOneConnectedOn. It unfolds to ChronallyHomotopicOn and ChronalHomotopyOn, so it carries both items of the definition.
paper_row.lean_ge_paper: Yes, under the binder's reading. Each clause of Def 2.13 is carried as printed: Γ is jointly continuous on [0,1]²; every Γ(t, ·), t ∈ [0,1], is a future curve from γ₀(0) to γ₀(1); Γ(0, ·) = γ₀ and Γ(1, ·) = γ₁ on [0,1]; and future one-connectedness quantifies over all p, q and all pairs of curves. The hypothesis 'time-oriented Lorentzian manifold with a continuous metric' is weakened to any causality on any topological space, and any open W (W = ⊤ is Sbierski's M). The one reading is 'future directed timelike curve' = 'future chronal curve of C' (Causal.Curves, DEC-6), the binder's reading for Def 2.14 too (ChronallySeparatedOn). So it is not literally ≥ Sbierski's Lorentzian notion. Under the C0 model every piecewise smooth timelike curve is a chronal curve, but not conversely. The ETT ∀ therefore ranges over more curves and the ETT ∃ admits more homotopies, and neither notion implies the other without a layer-3 comparison. Hence 'partial' (a reading), unmarked, as the other external Sbierski rows are (curation convention).

lemmas_for_the_keeper.standing: ℝ. Sbierski's printed Step 2.1 slice Γ(0, ·) = σ_{λ(0)} * λ (:572, :577, λ(0) = 0) on the 1 + 0-dimensional Minkowski line: not a chronal curve, whatever λ.

findings: Sbierski Thm 3.1 Step 2.1 (InexSchwarzschild2.tex:572, :575–579): the printed homotopy Γ(t, s) = (σ_{λ(t)} * λ|_{[t,1]})(s), with the concatenation split at s = 1/2 (:572) and λ(0) = 0, has degenerate end slices. At t = 0 the first half is σ_{λ(0)} = σ_0 ≡ 0, so Γ(0, ·) is constant on [0, 1/2]. It is therefore neither λ (Def 2.13 asks Γ(0, ·) = γ₀) nor a timelike curve. At t = 1, λ|_{[1,1]} is a point and cannot be 'linearly rescaled' to [0, 1] (:579), so Γ(1, ·) is constant on [1/2, 1]: neither σ_{λ(1)} nor timelike. In Lean: a chronal curve of a chronological open set is injective (Causal.Causality.ChronalCurveOn.injOn, TimelikeHomotopy.lean:161). The printed slice is not a chronal curve of the timelike line, the 1 + 0-dimensional Minkowski space, whatever λ (Causal.timelikeLine_not_chronalCurveOn_pause, :744). The conclusion of Step 2.1 still holds with the split at s = t: Γ(t, s) = σ_{λ(t)}(s/t) for 0 ≤ s ≤ t, λ(s) for t ≤ s ≤ 1, t ∈ (0, 1], and Γ(0, ·) = λ. This is continuous on [0,1]², since |σ_{λ(t)}(s/t)| ≤ |λ(t)| → 0, with Γ(1, ·) = σ_{λ(1)}. Every slice is a segment to λ(t) ≫ 0 followed by λ. This is not in Lean: it is a Minkowski fact, for T-loc-minkowski-future-one-connected.

Notational, minor. Def 2.13 is over [0, 1] (:383), but the proof of Prop 4.12 applies it to curves γᵢ : [t₀, t₁] → M_ext. It writes their endpoint conditions as γ₀(0) = γ₁(0), γ₀(1) = γ₁(1) (should be t₀, t₁) and the homotopy as Γ : [t₀,t₁] × [t₀,t₁] → M_ext, so the homotopy parameter also runs over [t₀, t₁] (:876). Thm 4.11 uses Γ : [0,1] × [y₀⁻, s] → M_int (:1623), whose curve σ runs 'from γ(x₀⁻)' over [y₀⁻, s] (x₀⁻ for y₀⁻). Both are the [0, 1] notion after an affine change of the parameters (CurveOn.comp_affine). Nothing here depends on them.
questions: Curves. I read 'future directed timelike curve' (Sbierski Def 2.1–2.2: piecewise smooth, timelike one-sided tangents in one cone) as a future chronal curve of C (Causal.Curves, DEC-6), the binder's reading, as for Def 2.14. Under the C0 model the ETT class is larger, so ETT future one-connectedness and Sbierski's do not imply each other a priori. For the consumers (Thm 3.1 Step 3, Thm 4.11's (FuturePastPreserving)) the ETT notion is what the confinement argument uses. Proving it of the models is harder at layer 3, though: Prop 4.12's proof (:876) projects piecewise smooth curves with speed < 1, which an ETT chronal curve need not be. The alternative, a model-supplied curve class as a parameter, was not taken.

Continuity. I took joint continuity on [0,1]², as printed, not the continuity of each slice. Slice continuity is automatic for chronal curves (CurveOn.continuousOn). Joint continuity is what Step 3's open–closed argument (:621) needs for the openness of I.

Direction. Def 2.13 says 'future directed' explicitly, so only chronal curves of C enter, not of C.dual (unlike Def 2.14's undirected 'timelike'). The past form is not needed: C.dual is future one-connected iff C is (Causal.Causality.dual_futureOneConnectedOn). The keeper's node can be two-sided.

Open set. FutureOneConnectedOn W is a property of W seen as a spacetime: chronal curves of W read only ≪_U, U ≤ W. It does not quantify over smaller open sets, because Sbierski's notion is not hereditary. Whether the keeper wants a hereditary variant is open; I wrote none.

Equivalence. The paper does not state that the relation is an equivalence. The target asked for it, and it holds on chronal curves only: reflexivity needs the curve to be chronal, the paper's own premise.
kb_proposals: Sbierski 1507.00601 Def 2.13 is Causality.ChronalHomotopyOn W Γ γ₀ γ₁ (jointly continuous on [0,1]², future chronal slices, fixed endpoints), ChronallyHomotopicOn (∃ Γ) and FutureOneConnectedOn / FutureOneConnected (CausalScaffold.TimelikeHomotopy, T-abs-timelike-homotopy). The relation is an equivalence on the chronal curves (chronallyHomotopicOn_equivalence); trans glues in t through ContinuousOn.union_of_isClosed on [0,1/2]×[0,1] ∪ [1/2,1]×[0,1].

Future one-connectedness is two-sided (dual_futureOneConnectedOn), reads ≪ only (futureOneConnectedOn_congr_lt), and passes through IsCausalIso (futureOneConnectedOn_iff, with e.opensCongr W) and through a ChartIso on W ≤ chartSource e (ChartIso.futureOneConnectedOn_iff, with chartImage e W). The timelike line is future one-connected on every open set (timelikeLine_futureOneConnectedOn).

On the timelike line the chronal curves of U over [a, b] are exactly the continuous strictly increasing maps of [a, b] into U (Causal.timelikeLine_chronalCurveOn_iff): a quick way to build chronal curves and homotopies of ℝ.

ETT-layer ChartIso transport of chronal curves, both ways: ChartIso.chronalCurveOn_image and ChartIso.chronalCurveOn_symm_image (CausalScaffold.TimelikeHomotopy). The older ChartIso.curveOn_symm sits in the model-layer Causal.Remarks.MassiveManifold and cannot be imported from layer 1.

A chronal curve of an open set with no x ≪ x is injective (Causality.ChronalCurveOn.injOn): a reparametrisation with a pause is never chronal there, so homotopies must not concatenate at a fixed split point when one piece can degenerate (Sbierski Step 2.1, timelikeLine_not_chronalCurveOn_pause).
